paper_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: What synthesis strategy and specific polymerization conditions were used to produce the PB-b-PY-1 through PB-b-PY-4 series of conjugated block copolymers?
qa_pairs.answer: The PB-b-PY-1 to PB-b-PY-4 series was synthesized using a one-pot polymerization method. The donor block (DB) polymerization time (T1) was varied at 0, 80, 160, and 240 minutes, respectively, while maintaining a total reaction time of 6 hours for all batches.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance parameters for the single-component organic solar cell based on the PB-b-PY-4 copolymer?
qa_pairs.answer: The PB-b-PY-4-based device achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.28%, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.92 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 21.87 mA cm^-2, and a fill factor (FF) of 66.0%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: How does the donor block polymerization time (T1) influence the molecular structure and optical properties of the PB-b-PY copolymers?
qa_pairs.answer: Increasing the T1 polymerization time leads to an increase in the conjugation length of the PBDB-T donor block. This structural change is evidenced by a higher intensity ratio of donor block absorption to acceptor block absorption (ID/IA) in the UV-Vis absorption spectra as T1 increases from 0 to 240 minutes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: Compare the crystal coherence length (CCL) of PB-b-PY-4 and PB-b-PY-2 as determined by GIWAXS, and explain what this indicates about the material's packing order.
qa_pairs.answer: PB-b-PY-4 exhibits a crystal coherence length (CCL) of 96.81 Å for the (100) lamellar stacking peak in the in-plane direction, which is significantly higher than the 39.767 Å observed for PB-b-PY-2. This indicates that increasing the donor block length in these conjugated block copolymers leads to a higher packing order of lamellar stacking.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: What evidence from charge recombination analysis suggests that PB-b-PY-4 has superior charge transport dynamics compared to PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3?
qa_pairs.answer: PB-b-PY-4 displays a lower trap-assisted recombination slope of 1.39 kT/q and a higher power-law alpha value of 0.983 for the relationship between Jsc and light intensity. These values indicate suppressed bimolecular and trap-assisted recombination losses in the PB-b-PY-4 device compared to the PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3 variants.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: What are the electron and hole mobilities for the PB-b-PY-4 material, and what does the ratio between them suggest?
qa_pairs.answer: PB-b-PY-4 has a hole mobility (μh) of 4.22 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and an electron mobility (μe) of 4.24 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. Since the μh/μe ratio is approximately 1, the material exhibits balanced charge carrier transport.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: How does the photostability of PB-b-PY-4 compare to PB-b-PY-2 and PB-b-PY-3 after extended light-soaking?
qa_pairs.answer: PB-b-PY-4 shows superior photostability, retaining 87% of its initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 340 hours of continuous one-sun illumination. In contrast, PB-b-PY-3 and PB-b-PY-2 retained only 72% and 63% of their initial PCE, respectively, over the same period.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block

qa_pairs.question: Why does the steady-state photoluminescence (PL) quenching efficiency increase from 71.6% in PB-b-PY-2 to 85.4% in PB-b-PY-4?
qa_pairs.answer: The increase in PL quenching efficiency is attributed to the longer conjugation length of the donor block in PB-b-PY-4. As the donor block conjugation length increases, the charge transfer from the acceptor block to the donor block becomes more effective, leading to higher quenching.
qa_pairs.source_title: Over 13% Efficient Single-Component Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Adjusting the Conjugated-Length of Intermediate PBDB-T Block
